# Geometry, rays and beams

Basic objects: everything with a position and a direction, single rays and bundles of rays.

### Geom_Object

```python
Geom_Object(name='unnamed', **kwargs)
```

Base class of all objects with a position and an orientation in space.

Stores the position <pos>, the orientation <normal> and the <name>. Setting
<normal> automatically adjusts the inner coordinate system <_axes> and calls
the helper functions <_pos_changed> and <_axes_changed>, which composite
objects like Beam or Composition use to move their sub-objects along.

Provides the <draw_dict> with all important keyword arguments for drawing; it
can be extended arbitrarily and is passed to the draw routines. Unknown
constructor keywords produce a warning; `pos` and `normal` are not accepted in
the constructor, set them afterwards.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `angle_to(obj, axis=None)` | computes the angle to the normal of an other GeomObj <obj> |
| `class_name(cls)` | Return the name of the class of the object, e.g. "Mirror". |
| `draw()` | function to display the object checks whether freecad is available as backend and then calls the corresponding draw function |
| `draw_freecad()` | if FreeCAD is present, calls the corresponding drawing function from freecad_models, normally returns a reference to the corresponding FreeCAD object |
| `draw_text()` | if FreeCAD is not available, the object will be "drawn" into the console. "drawn", i.e. all relevant parameters from the <draw_dict> will be by text, returns the text as str |
| `get_axes()` | returns the own coordinate system _axes as 3x3 matrix where the x,y,z-vectors are column vectors |
| `get_coordinate_system()` | returns normal (x), perpendicular1 (y) and perpendicular2 (z) as 3 vectors (transposed to self.get_axes) |
| `get_geom()` | returns the so-called geom, simply a tuple of <pos> and <axes>, important for the geometric definition of most objects |
| `normal` (property) | Beschreibt die Ausrichtung (= interne x-Achse) des GeomObject als 3D-numpy- float-array mit Betrag 1 stellt über Setter und Getter sicher, dass nur Kopien übergeben werden, der Vektor stehts normiert wird und das die _axes aktualisiert wird |
| `pos` (property) | beschreibt die Position des GeomObject als 3D-numpy-float-array stellt über Setter und Getter sicher, dass nur Kopien übergeben werden und das _pos_changed aufgrufen wird |
| `rotate(vec, phi)` | rotates the object with respect to vec by the angle phi Parameters ---------- vec : 3D vector Space direction around which is rotated, must not be normalized phi : angle in radians |
| `set_axes(new_axes)` | Set the own coordinate system to <new_axes> and call _axes_changed. |
| `set_geom(geom)` | Set (pos, axes) from <geom> by calling the corresponding setters. |
| `update_draw_dict()` | is usually called for the draw_routines and can update the most important key word arguments of <draw_dict> if they have been changed (e.g. self.radius of have been changed (e.g. self.radius of Curved_Mirror). |

### Ray

```python
Ray(**kwargs)
```

*Inherits from:* `Geom_Object`

A single ray: position <pos>, direction <normal> and a <length> for drawing.

Inherits from Geom_Object. Default: position (0, 0, 80), direction (1, 0, 0),
wavelength 660 nm (0.00066 mm).


**Methods**

- endpoint(), intersection_with(element), h_alpha_to(element),
- h_alpha_theta_to(element), from_h_alpha_theta(h, alpha, theta, element)

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `endpoint()` | Return the end point pos + length * normal of the ray. |
| `from_h_alpha_theta(h, alpha, theta, element)` | Set the geometry of the ray so that it has the geometrical parameters <h, alpha, theta> with respect to <element>. |
| `h_alpha_theta_to(element)` | Return (h, alpha) of geometrical optics when the ray hits <element>, and the angle <theta> of the point of incidence around the axis of the element, measured from its z-axis (uses the intersection). |
| `h_alpha_to(element)` | Return the parameters (h, alpha) of geometrical optics when the ray hits <element> (uses the intersection). |
| `intersection(element, set_length=True)` | Calculates the intersection point of the ray with a plane given by a Geom_Object (e.g a thin lens). |
| `update_draw_dict()` | Add the length of the ray to <draw_dict>. |

### Beam

```python
Beam(radius=1, angle=0, name='NewBeam', wavelength=0.00103, ray_count=2, **kwargs)
```

*Inherits from:* `Geom_Object`

Base class for a group of rays (you don't say!)
special funcitoins: make_square_distribution(radius=1, ray_count=5)
make_circular_distribution(radius=1, ray_count=5)
average_divegence = ?

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `draw_freecad()` | Draw the beam in FreeCAD. |
| `focal_length()` | Return the distance to the apex of the beam cone. |
| `get_all_rays(by_reference=False)` | Return all rays of the beam, the inner ray first. |
| `inner_ray()` | Return a copy of the inner (central) ray of the beam. |
| `length()` | Return the propagation length of the beam (length of the inner ray). |
| `make_cone_distribution(ray_count=2)` | Distribute the rays on a cone: one inner ray on the axis and <ray_count>-1 outer rays on a circle with the beam radius and the divergence angle of the beam. |
| `outer_rays()` | Return copies of all rays except the inner ray. |
| `override_rays(rays)` | setzt die rays neu, muss man eventuell aufpassen, mal sehen |
| `radius_angle()` | Compute the beam cone (radius r and opening angle alpha) from the inner and outer ray of the beam. |
| `set_length(x)` | Set the length of all rays of the beam to <x>. |
| `set_ray_color(color)` | Set the drawing color of all rays, e.g. (1.0, 0.0, 0.0). |
| `set_wavelength(wl)` | Set the wavelength <wl> (in mm) of the beam and of all its rays. |
| `update_draw_dict()` | Add length, radius and angle of the beam cone to <draw_dict>. |
| `wavelength()` | Return the wavelength of the beam (wavelength of the inner ray) in mm. |

### CircularRayBeam

```python
CircularRayBeam(radius=1, name='NewBeam', wavelength=0.00103, ring_number=2, **kwargs)
```

*Inherits from:* `Beam`

Beam whose rays are arranged on concentric rings (for spot diagrams).


**Parameters**

- `radius` (float)
  Radius of the outermost ring in mm.
- `ring_number` (int)
  Number of rings around the central ray.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `make_circular_distribution(ring_number=2)` | Let the group of rays follow the circular distribution The radius of circle equals the radius of ray group Parameters ---------- ring_number : int(>0).​ [Click and drag to move] The number of the rings around the center. That is going to determine the density of ray. |

### Gaussian_Beam

```python
Gaussian_Beam(radius=10, angle=0.02, wavelength=0.00103, name='NewGassian', **kwargs)
```

*Inherits from:* `Ray`

Beam described by its complex Gaussian beam parameter q.


**Parameters**

- `radius` (float)
  Beam radius in mm at the position of the beam.
- `angle` (float)
  Half divergence angle in rad (negative: converging).
- `wavelength` (float)
  Wavelength in mm.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `divergence()` | Return the angle of the 1/e^2 envelope at the start of the beam. |
| `draw_freecad()` | Draw the Gaussian beam in FreeCAD. |
| `draw_gaussian_profile(center_intensity=2, norm=True)` | Plot the transverse intensity profile at the start of the beam with matplotlib. |
| `get_all_rays()` | Return a list with one ray on the beam axis (same geom, wavelength and length). |
| `inner_ray()` | Return the ray on the beam axis. |
| `radius()` | Return the beam radius w(z) at the start of the beam in mm. |
| `set_length(length)` | Set the propagation length of the Gaussian beam (used by next_beam). |
| `transform_to_cone_beam()` | Return a cone Beam with the same radius, divergence, geom and length. |
| `update_draw_dict()` | Add name, wavelength, propagation length and geom to <draw_dict>. |
| `waist()` | Return the waist radius w0 = sqrt(wavelength/pi * Im(q)) in mm. |

### RainbowBeam

```python
RainbowBeam(name='NewRainbow', wavelength=0.00103, bandwidth=1e-05, ray_count=11, thickness=2, **kwargs)
```

*Inherits from:* `Beam`

Group of rays with different wavelengths, used for dispersive setups.


**Parameters**

- `wavelength` (float)
  Central wavelength in mm (default 1030e-6, i.e. 1030 nm).
- `bandwidth` (float)
  Full spectral width in mm (default 10e-6, i.e. 10 nm).
- `ray_count` (int)
  Number of rays, the middle ray has the central wavelength.
- `thickness` (float)
  Line thickness used when drawing the rays.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `make_rainbow_distribution(ray_count=11)` | Create <ray_count> rays on the beam axis with wavelengths spread over the bandwidth. |

### Ray_Distribution

```python
Ray_Distribution(name='NewRayDist', radius=3, steps=3, angle=0.05, **kwargs)
```

*Inherits from:* `SquareBeam`

creates a ray distribution in all directions with opening angle <angle> and
radius <radius> consisting of steps^3 + 1 rays

### SquareBeam

```python
SquareBeam(radius=1, name='NewBeam', wavelength=0.00103, ray_in_line=3, **kwargs)
```

*Inherits from:* `Beam`

Beam whose rays form a square grid (for spot diagrams and aberrations).


**Parameters**

- `radius` (float)
  Half the width of the square in mm.
- `ray_in_line` (int)
  Number of rays per line of the grid.

| Member | Description |
|---|---|
| `make_square_distribution(ray_in_line=3)` | Let the group of rays follow the square distribution The width of square equals 2*radius of ray group Parameters ---------- ray_in_line : int(>0) rays in a line.That is going to determine the density of ray. |
